senses.gloss:
रुद् 1. रुद् [cf. rt. 1. रु], cl. 2. P. रोदिति
(Ved. also cl. 6. रुदति, ep. also A. रुदते),
Impf. अरोदीत् or अरोदत् (Pāṇ. VII. 3, 98, 99; 1st
sing. अरोदम्, 3rd pl. अरुदन्), Impv. रोदितु (2nd
sing. रुदिहि), Perf. रुरोद (ep. रुरुदे), 2nd Fut.
रोदिष्यति (Ved. रोत्स्यति), Aor. अरोदीत् (3rd pl.
अरोदिषुस्) or अरुदत्, रोदितुम्, to weep, cry, shed
tears, wail, lament; to bewail, deplore; to roar, howl:
Pass. रुद्यते, Aor. अरोदि: Caus. रोदयति, -यि-
तुम्, Aor. अरूरुदत्, to cause to weep or lament:
Desid. रुरुदिषति: Intens. रोरुद्यते, रोरोत्ति, to
weep very much; [cf. perhaps Gr. ὀῤῥωδέω; Lat.
rud-o; Old Germ. riuzan; Angl. Sax. reotan;
Lith. raudoju; Slav. rudajun.]

2. रुद्, त्, त्, त्, weeping, crying, lamenting [cf.
अघ-र्˚]; (त्), f. cry, wail, lamentation; sound,
noise; grief; pain, affliction; disease.

रुदत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, weeping, crying,
wailing, bewailing; (अन्ती), f. a species of small shrub
(= रुदन्तिका).

रुदथ, अस्, m. a child, a pupil, scholar; a dog;
a cock.

रुदन, अम्, n. the act of crying, weeping,
lamentation.

रुदन्तिका, f. ‘the weeper,’ epithet of a species
of small succulent shrub (= अमृत-स्रवा).

रुदमान, अस्, आ, अम्, weeping, wailing, lament-
ing.
रुदित्वा, ind. having wept, having lamented.
रुद्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being bewailed.

रुद्र, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 22.
fr. rt. 1. रुद् above; according to others fr. rt. 1. रु
+ द्र fr. rt. 2. द्रु, to run; connected with रोदस्,
q. v., and perhaps with रुधिर), crying, howling,
roaring, one who cries or roars, dreadful, horrible,
terrific, awful; great, large; (according to the fanciful
etymologies of native writers, the following meanings
are also assigned to this word), driving away evil;
running about and roaring; praiseworthy, to be
praised, (according to Naigh. III. 16) = स्तोतृ, a
praiser, panegyrist, worshipper; (अस्), m. ‘the Roarer’
or ‘Howler,’ N. of the god of tempests and father
of the Rudras or Maruts, (originally perhaps the
mere personified roaring of the storms, but as the
crackling or raging of fire may resemble the sound
of wind, so in the Veda the god of storms is some-
times identified with the god of fire; though gene-
rally represented as a destroying deity whose terrible
shafts bring death or disease on men and cattle, he
is also addressed as benevolent and auspicious [शिव],
and is even supposed to have a healing efficacy from
his chasing away vapours and purifying the atmo-
sphere; hence he has various epithets in the Veda,
such as ‘multiform,’ ‘terrible as a wild beast,’ ‘tawny-
coloured,’ ‘wearing braided hair’ [कपर्दिन्], ‘ce-
lestial boar,’ ‘armed with a strong bow and fleet
arrows,’ ‘cause of prosperity to man and beast,’ ‘pos-
sessor of healing remedies,’ ‘greatest of physicians,’
&c.; he is of course ruler of the Rudras, who are
the same as the storm winds, more usually called
Maruts, and who are often associated with Indra [see
मरुत्]: in the later mythology the epithet शिव,
[]
‘propitious,’ which does not occur as a name in the
Veda, was employed as the real name of the destroy-
ing deity, being at first applied as an euphemism to
propitiate him: moreover the character of the deity
lost its special connection with storms, and developed
into a personification of the destroying principle
generally, though even the Epic and Purānic Śiva
was regarded as the generator as well as destroyer:
moreover a new class of beings, described as eleven
in number, though still called Rudras, took the
place of the original Rudras or Maruts: in the Veda
only three groupings of deities into classes appear to
be recognised, Indra belonging to the Vasus, Varuṇa
to the Ādityas, and Rudra to the Rudras or Maruts;
but in Manu XI. 221. the Maruts are enumerated
as a fourth group, being there distinguished from
the eleven Rudras: in Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 7. Rudra
is said to have sprung from Brahmā's forehead, and
to have afterwards separated himself into a figure
half male and half female, the former portion sepa-
rating again into the eleven Rudras, who were so
called because they ‘ran about crying aloud’ [रुद-
नाद् द्रावणाच्-च, cf. rts. 1. रुद्, 2. द्रु]; hence
these later Rudras are sometimes regarded as inferior
manifestations of Śiva, and most of their names are
also names of Śiva; these names are variously given
in the different Purāṇas; those of the Vāyu are
Ajaikapād, Ahvi-bradhna, Hara, Nir-ṛta, Īśvara,
Bhuvana, Aṅgāraka, Ardha-ketu, Mṛtyu, Sarpa,
Kapālin: according to other accounts the Rudras are
represented as children of Kaśyapa and Surabhī or of
Brahmā and Surabhī or of Bhūta and Su-rūpā); a
form or manifestation or N. of Śiva (in the later
mythology, as explained above; according to the
Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 8. Rudra is one of the eight forms
of Śiva; he is elsewhere reckoned among the Dik-
pālas as regent of the north-east quarter); a symbo-
lical expression for the number eleven (from the
eleven Rudras, see above); a mystical epithet of
the letter ए; Calotropis Gigantea; N. of various
persons; of a lexicographer; of a poet; of a king;
(आस्), m. pl. the Rudras (described above); an
abbreviated expression for the texts or hymns ad-
dressed to the Rudras [cf. रुद्र-जप]; (आ), f.,
N. of a wife of Vasu-deva; of a daughter of Rau-
drāśva; = रुद्र-जटा; (ई), f. a kind of lute or
guitar; [cf. रुद्र-वीणा; cf. perhaps also Gr. λύρα.]
—रुद्र-कलश, अम्, n. ‘Rudra's vessel,’ a parti-
cular kind of pot or vessel used in making oblations
to the planets.
—रुद्र-कवीन्द्र (˚वि-इन्˚), अस्, m.
a proper N. (= रुद्र-भट्ट).
—रुद्र-काली, f. a
form of Durgā.
—रुद्र-कोटि, इस्, f., N. of a place
of pilgrimage.
—रुद्र-कोष, अस्, m., N. of a
lexicon by Rudra.
—रुद्र-गण, अस्, m., Ved.
‘Rudra-class,’ the troop of beings called Rudras,
(see under रुद्र.)
—रुद्र-गर्भ, अस्, m. ‘Ru-
dra's offspring,’ N. of Agni.
—रुद्र-गीत, अम्, आ,
n. f. the song of Rudra (in which Agastya repeats
a dialogue between himself and Rudra).
—रुद्र-
चण्डिक, epithet of a particular text or formula.
—रुद्र-चण्डी, f. a form of Durgā; N. of a
section in the Rudra-yāmala.
—रुद्र-चन्द्र, अस्,
m., N. of a king.
—रुद्र-च्छत्त्र, अस्, m. a
proper N.
—रुद्र-ज, अस्, m. (according to some)
अम्, n. ‘produced from Rudra or Śiva,’ quicksilver
(supposed to be the semen of Śiva).
—रुद्र-जटा,
f. ‘Rudra's hair,’ N. of a species of creeper.
—रु-
द्र-जप, अस्, m., N. of a particular prayer or
hymn addressed to Rudra.
—रुद्र-जपन, अम्,
n. the recitation of the Rudra-japa in a low tone.
—रुद्र-जापक, अस्, इका, अम्, or रुद्र-जापिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, one who recites the Rudra-japa in a low
tone.
—रुद्र-जाप्य, अम्, n., N. of a particular
hymn or prayer extracted from the Vājasaneyi-saṃ-
hitā and addressed to Rudra.
—रुद्र-तनय, अस्,
m. ‘Rudra's son,’ N. of the third black Vāsudeva;
of Punishment; epithet of a sword.
—रुद्र-त्व,
अम्, n. the being Rudra.
—रुद्र-दत्त, अस्, m.,
N. of an author; of a work on medicine.
—रुद्र-
दामन्, आ, m., N. of a king.
—रुद्र-देव, अस्,
m., N. of various persons; of the author of the
[]
Yayāti-carita; of the author of a commentary on
the Prabodha-candrodaya.
—रुद्र-धर, अस्, m.,
N. of an author.
—रुद्र-न्याय-वाचस्पति-भट्-
टाचार्य (˚त-आच्˚), अस्, m., N. of an author (=
रुद्र-भट्टाचार्य).
—रुद्र-पण्डित, अस्, m.,
N. of an author (= रुद्र-सूरि).
—रुद्र-पत्नी,
f. Rudra's wife, the goddess Durgā; linseed, Linum
Usitatissimum.
—रुद्र-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of
a work by Paraśu-rāma.
—रुद्र-पाल, अस्, m. a
proper N.
—रुद्र-पुत्र, अस्, m. Rudra's son, a
patronymic of the twelfth Manu; [cf. रुद्र-सा-
वर्णि.]
—रुद्र-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a province.
—रुद्र-पूजन, अम्, n. or रुद्र-पूजा, f. ‘wor-
ship of Rudra,’ N. of a work.
—रुद्र-प्रताप,
अस्, m., N. of a king (= प्रताप-रुद्र).
—रुद्र-
प्रयाग, अस्, m., N. of the sacred place where the
river Mandākinī joins the Ganges.
—रुद्र-प्रिया,
f. ‘dear to Rudra,’ epithet of Terminalia Chebula;
the goddess Pārvatī.
—रुद्र-बलि, इस्, m. an oblation
of meat &c. presented to the Rudras.
—रुद्र-
भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Śṛṅgāra-
tilaka (= रुद्रट); of the author of a commentary
on the Vaidya-jīvana; = रुद्र-कवीन्द्र.
—रुद्र-
भट्टाचार्य (˚ट-आच्˚), अस्, m., N. of an author
and commentator.
—रुद्र-भाष्य, अम्, n., N.
of a work by Ahobala.
—रुद्र-भू, ऊस्, or रुद्र-
भूमि, इस्, f. ‘Rudra's ground,’ a cemetery.
—रुद्र-
भूति, इस्, m., N. of a preceptor (having the patro-
nymic Drāhyāyaṇi).
—रुद्र-भैरवी, f. a form
of Durgā.
—रुद्र-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of
Rudra, having the essence of Rudra.
—रुद्र-
महा-देवी, f., N. of the wife of king Govinda-
canda.
—रुद्र-यज्ञ, अस्, m. an oblation or sacri-
fice offered to Rudra.
—रुद्र-यामल, अम्, n.,
N. of a Tantra work in the form of a dialogue
between Bhairava and Bhairavī.
—रुद्र-राय, अस्,
m., N. of a king.
—रुद्र-राशि, इस्, m. a proper N.
—रुद्र-रोदन, अम्, n. ‘Rudra's tears,’ i. e. gold.
—रुद्र-रोमन्, आ, f., N. of one of the Mātṛs
attending upon Skanda.
—रुद्र-लटा, f. = रुद्र-
जटा.
—रुद्र-लोक, अस्, m. Rudra's world.
—रु-
द्र-वट, N. of a Tīrtha.
—रुद्र-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, Ved. having Rudra or the Rudras.
—रुद्रवद्-
गण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. surrounded by the Rudra
troop.
—रुद्र-वर्तनि, ई, m. du. ‘proceeding on
terrible roads,’ N. of the Aśvins, (Sāy. = रोदन-
शील-मार्गौ or स्तूयमान-मार्गौ.)
—रुद्र-
विंशति, इस्, f. epithet of the last twenty years in the
Jupiter cycle of sixty years.
—रुद्र-विधान, अम्,
n., N. of a work.
—रुद्र-वीणा, f. epithet of a
particular religious observance.
—रुद्र-शर्मन्, आ,
m., N. of a Brāhman.
—रुद्र-सम्प्रदायिन्, इनस्,
m. pl., N. of a sect.
—रुद्र-सरस्, अस्, n., N. of a
lake.
—रुद्र-सर्ग, अस्, m. Rudra's creation; the
creation of the eleven Rudras.
—रुद्र-सामन्, अ,
n., N. of a particular Sāman.
—रुद्र-सावर्णि, इस्,
m., N. of the twelfth Manu; [cf. रुद्र-पुत्र,
मनु.]
—रुद्रसावर्णिक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging
or relating to Rudra-sāvarṇi, being under Rudra-
sāvarṇi.
—रुद्र-सिंह, अस्, m. a proper N.
—रु-
द्र-सुन्दरी, f., N. of a goddess.
—रुद्र-सू, ऊस्,
f. a mother of eleven children.
—रुद्र-सूक्त, अम्,
n., N. of a particular hymn.
—रुद्र-सूरि, इस्, m.,
N. of an author.
—रुद्र-सृष्टि, इस्, f. Rudra's
creation; the creation of the eleven Rudras; [cf.
रुद्र-सर्ग.]
—रुद्र-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a
warrior.
—रुद्र-सोम, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman.
—रुद्र-स्कन्द, अस्, m., N. of a commentator.
—रुद्र-स्वर्ग, अस्, m. Rudra's heaven.
—रुद्र-
स्वामिन्, ई, m. a proper N.
—रुद्र-हिमालय, अस्,
m., N. of a peak of the Himālaya mountains.
—रुद्र-हूति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. (according to Mahī-
dhara on Vājasaneyi-s. XXXVIII. 16) being invoked
by praisers or worshippers.
—रुद्र-हृदय, अम्,
n., N. of an Upaniṣad.
—रुद्राक्रीड (˚र-आक्˚),
अस्, m. ‘Rudra's play-ground,’ a cemetery, place
where dead bodies are burnt or buried (Rudra being
supposed to dance and sport in such places at evening
twilight).
—रुद्राक्ष (˚र-अक्˚), अस्, m. ‘Rudra-
eyed,’ a kind of tree, Elæocarpus Ganitrus; (अम्),
n. the berry of this tree (used for rosaries); a rosary;
[]
N. of an Upaniṣad, (the gender here and in the preced-
ing sense is doubtful.)
—रुद्राक्ष-माला, f. a rosary
made of Rudrākṣa berries.
—रुद्राचार्य (˚र-आच्˚),
अस्, m. a proper N.
—रुद्राध्याय (˚र-अध्˚), अस्,
m. epithet of particular prayers addressed to Rudra.
—रुद्राध्यायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, one who recites or
repeats the above prayers.
—रुद्रायण (˚र-अय्˚),
अस्, m., N. of a king of Roruka.
—रुद्रारि (˚र-
अरि), इस्, m. Rudra's enemy; N. of Kāma-deva;
(इस्, इस्, इ), having Rudra for an enemy, hostile to
Rudra.
—रुद्रावर्त (˚र-आव्˚), N. of a place of
pilgrimage.
—रुद्रावसृष्ट (˚र-अव्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, Ved. let go or hurled by Rudra.
—रुद्रावास
(˚र-आव्˚), अस्, m. Rudra's abode, i. e. Kāśi or Be-
nares.
—रुद्रैकादशिनी (˚र-एक्˚), f. the eleven
Rudra hymns.
—रुद्रोपनिषद् (˚र-उप्˚), त्, f., N.
of two Upaniṣads.
—रुद्रोपस्थ (˚र-उप्˚), अस्,
m. ‘Rudra's generative organ,’ N. of a mountain.
रुद्र रुद्र. See p. 849, col. 1.
रुद्रक, अस्, m. a proper N.

रुद्रट, अस्, m. an abbreviated form of Rudra-
bhaṭṭa.

रुद्राणी, f. Rudra's wife, the goddess Durgā;
epithet of a girl eleven years of age, in whom men-
struation has not yet commenced, representing the
goddess Durgā at the Durgā festival.
रुद्ध रुद्ध. See col. 2.

रुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, stopped, checked, impeded,
restrained, obstructed, suppressed, opposed; held,
withheld; kept, kept back; shut, closed, shut up,
secured; invested, besieged, blockaded; shut in,
enclosed, confined, surrounded, begirt, fenced in;
covered, covered up; (अस्), m., N. of a town; (आ),
f. a siege.
—रुद्ध-गिर्, ईर्, ईर्, ईर्, having the
utterance choked or impeded.
—रुद्ध-प्रवाह,
अस्, आ, अम्, having the stream obstructed.
—रुद्ध-
मूत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having the urine suppressed;
suffering from retention of urine.
रुद्धक, अम्, n. citron, (perhaps for रुचक.)

रुद्ध्वा, ind. having stopped or checked, having
restrained or obstructed.
